summary: This work demonstrates a Raman-assisted cross-Kerr interaction between microwave photons in two superconducting cavities without populating the mediating transmon coupler, achieving a controlled-phase gate with ~5% infidelity and performing bosonic parity checks that preserve the code space. The engineered coupling is $g_{ab}/2\pi \approx 90$ kHz (two orders of magnitude stronger than the residual always-on interaction), enabling deterministic entanglement generation and opening a pathway toward fault-tolerant bosonic quantum computing.
motivation: Direct nonlinear coupling between harmonic oscillators is essential for deterministic entanglement and universal quantum computation with bosonic modes, yet existing parametric schemes populate excited states of the nonlinear coupler, introducing decoherence and leakage from the protected code space.
method: An off-resonant microwave drive at the coherent exchange frequency between the cavities and coupler activates virtual transitions via second-order Raman processes; this is derived via Schrieffer–Wolff transformation and yields an effective Hamiltonian $\hat{H}_{\text{eff}}/\hbar = g_{ab}\hat{a}^\dagger\hat{a}\hat{b}^\dagger\hat{b}|g\rangle\langle g|$ with strength $g_{ab} \approx g_1^2 \Delta/(\Delta - \chi_b)/(\Delta + \chi_b)$ at detuning $\Delta/2\pi = -6$ MHz and exchange rate $g_1/2\pi = 0.8$ MHz.
result: Controlled-Z gates in the 0/1 subspace operate in $\approx 5.2$ µs with average infidelity per gate of 4.2 ± 0.3% (limited primarily by driven cavity decoherence); in the 0/2 subspace, gates run in 1.94 µs with 1.9 ± 0.1% infidelity post-selected on even parity; bosonic parity checks enhance storage lifetime from $T_1 = 763 ± 11$ µs to $1173 ± 41$ µs when post-selected, preserving Wigner negativity of $|2\rangle$ against photon loss.
